_readme: PENDING WEB TOKEN DRIFT. THE LEDGER IS EMPTY, AND THAT IS THE GOAL STATE.
apps/web/app/design-system/tokens.css and apps/web/public/design/tokens.css
were not updated by the WCAG AA token repair (jits-anbc), so until jits-ozvd
landed they legitimately disagreed with apps/mobile/lib/tokens.ts on 21 tokens
each, and this file recorded exactly how. jits-ozvd applied the same repair to
both web mirrors; every one of those 21 entries per mirror is gone because the
divergence it described is gone. All four mirrors (two mobile, two web) now
resolve to identical values for all 17 mapped tokens in both themes.
With mirrors empty, apps/mobile/__tests__/lib/tokens-mirror-drift.test.ts gates
the web mirrors exactly as strictly as the brand file: ANY divergence from
lib/tokens.ts fails, because no divergence is covered here.
Shape: mirrors[<path>]["<theme> <css custom property>"] = the value that mirror
CURRENTLY resolves to, normalised, or "(not declared)" when the mirror does not
declare the token at all. The EXPECTED value is deliberately not recorded here;
it is read from lib/tokens.ts at run time, so there is exactly one source of
truth for what a token is supposed to be.
DO NOT add an entry here to silence a failing token. An entry is only ever
correct for a divergence that is deliberate AND temporary, i.e. a palette
change that has landed on one platform and has a tracked issue to land on the
other. Anything else is a mirror that needs fixing. The ledger is an exact
match, not a licence: an entry whose divergence has been resolved fails just as
loudly as an unrecorded one.
This file and the pending branch in tokens-mirror-drift.test.ts can both be
deleted outright once no future split-platform token change is expected; they
are kept because that mechanism is the only thing that let the mobile suite
stay green and non-blind across a two-session palette migration.
Recorded 2026-09-18 against the palette merged at af87d69; emptied by jits-ozvd.
